about: Inputs for the population-level test (new lunar craters vs impactor flux x crater scaling). Source IDs refer to audit/research/lit_session5/population_rates.md (R01-R26), which records identity, status and reading depth. The survey exposure and counts are DERIVED by digitising the open Fig. 2 of Speyerer et al. (2016, Nature 538, 215; R01); the paper's Methods (paywalled) were not read. Every step of the digitised cumulative curve falls on an integer count under one exposure value, which is the internal-consistency check.

survey.label: LROC NAC temporal pairs 2009-2015 (Speyerer et al. 2016)
survey.source: R01 Fig. 2 (digitised); population_rates.md table B1 rows 8-10

flux.label: Brown et al. (2002) bolide flux, transferred to the Moon
flux.earth_cumulative_per_yr: N(>E) = 3.70 E^-0.90, E in kilotons TNT (1 kt = 4.185e12 J)
flux.normalisation_note: Factor 1/4 (NEOMOD3 finds the D>10 m flux ~4x below the bolide estimate, R12 s5.4) to x2 (luminous-efficiency envelope 5-20%, R06).
flux.applicable_range_note: Fit supported for impactor diameters ~1-10 m; 7-40 m lunar craters need ~0.1-0.6 m bodies, so the law is extrapolated. Lunar flash flux at 30 g (Suggs et al. 2014, R08) is within ~30% of the extrapolation.
flux.source: R06 p.295 eq. (2) (read in full from an author copy); R09 Table 3 (Earth/Moon per-area 1.58)
